summary: A 38-line pilot sketch of Champollion's (2016) intersective theory of noun coordination in Winter-style flexible Boolean semantics: conjunction as generalized intersection fixed at type ((e->Prop)->Prop) (INT/and), existential raising of predicates to quantifiers (ER), the minimality/witness-set operator (MIN), an existential determiner over sets of predicates (a), and a distributive predication operator over set-pluralities (PDIST). The paper's running examples 'a man and a woman dated' (collective, via the Parameter date) and 'a man and a woman had a beer' (distributive, via PDIST) are assembled, type-checked with Check, and unfolded with Eval cbv — but nothing is proved: the file contains no Theorem, no Qed, and its closing comment concedes that choice closure (the operator the theory needs for its headline hybrid readings) is left undone ('needs probably an inductive type').

sources.citation: Champollion, L. (2016). Ten men and women got married today: Noun coordination and the intersective theory of conjunction. Journal of Semantics 33(3):561-622.
Winter, Y. (2001). Flexibility Principles in Boolean Semantics. MIT Press. (origin of the ER/MIN/choice-closure operator inventory that Champollion 2016 adopts)

definitions_mapped.coq: INT / and := fun P Q X => P X /\ Q X (line 5-7)
definitions_mapped.source: conjunction as cross-categorial generalized intersection (Partee & Rooth), the core of Champollion 2016's intersective theory
definitions_mapped.note: fixed at the single type ((e->Prop)->Prop) rather than the source's cross-categorial schema over all conjoinable types

definitions_mapped.coq: ER := fun P Q => exists x, In_s (intersection P Q) x (line 3)
definitions_mapped.source: existential raising of a predicate to a quantifier (Winter's E, adopted in Champollion 2016)

definitions_mapped.coq: MIN := fun Q P => Q P /\ forall P', strict_included P' P -> ~ Q P' (line 18)
definitions_mapped.source: the minimality/witness operator restricting a quantifier to its minimal witness sets (Champollion 2016, after Winter)

definitions_mapped.coq: a := fun P Q => exists X, P X /\ Q X (line 19)
definitions_mapped.note: rendered as a determiner over sets of predicates; set-pluralities stand in for the source's plural individuals (the source's own set-based setting makes this mild)

definitions_mapped.coq: PDIST := fun P' P => ~ Empty_set P /\ included P P' (line 29)
definitions_mapped.source: distributive predication over a plurality (the D/distributivity operator)
collective predicate 'dated' and the distributive VP 'have a beer'
definitions_mapped.note: collective predicate left as an unanalyzed constant; have_a_beer lexicalized non-compositionally (the file's own comment flags this)

definitions_mapped.source: choice closure (Winter's C), required for Champollion 2016's headline hybrid readings such as 'ten men and women got married'
definitions_mapped.note: closing comment line 38: 'Choice closure seems doable but not as straightforward ... needs probably an inductive type'

definitions_mapped.source: the numeral 'ten' and the paper's title example 'Ten men and women got married today'

determination_rationale: Mechanically, rubric row 3 applies because only a partial formalization exists — but the rationale must be read as provisional: the partiality is set by the pilot's incompleteness (zero theorems, choice closure unattempted), not by a diagnosed resistance of the theory. What is present (ER, INT, MIN) embeds essentially verbatim into Coq's set-of-predicates setting, suggesting a fuller attempt could raise the theory to determination 1-2; the one concrete obstacle the file itself names — choice closure 'needs probably an inductive type' — is a class (iv) missing-native-structure artifact (a choice operator has no direct impredicative encoding). A larger sibling file champollion_full.v exists in extras/ and should be audited before the theory-level determination is fixed.
